_comment: The tool registry: what exists, what the model is told, and what needs a human. Tool names, argument names and descriptions follow opencode (MIT). config/workflow.yaml decides which of these a workflow may use.

bash.description: execute one shell command inside the workspace; returns the exit code and the output

timeout.description: seconds to allow; 0 or omitted uses the workflow default, maximum 120

bash.title: Run {command}

read.description: read a text file in the workspace, one page of numbered lines; use offset to page through a long file

path.description: file path relative to the workspace

read.title: Read {path}

write.description: create or overwrite a text file in the workspace

path.description: file path relative to the workspace

write.title: Write {path}

edit.description: replace exact text in a workspace file; prefer this over rewriting a whole file

newString.description: replacement text, which must differ from oldString

edit.title: Edit {path}

glob.description: find workspace files whose path matches a pattern, for example "*.py"

path.description: subfolder to search, default the whole workspace

glob.title: Glob "{pattern}"

grep.description: search the contents of workspace files with a regular expression

path.description: subfolder to search, default the whole workspace

include.description: only search files matching this pattern, for example "*.py"

grep.title: Grep "{pattern}"

webfetch.description: fetch a public http(s) URL and return its text; HTML is converted to plain text
webfetch.title: Fetch {url}

websearch.description: search the web and return a title, url and snippet per result; use it for anything beyond your knowledge
websearch.title: Search "{query}"
